slides.title: My tests never ran. **For months.**
slides.sub: One line of config read like a promise. It was a filter.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout stands guard proudly at a castle gate wearing a tiny helmet and holding a spear, saluting, while right behind him a long line of little carts quietly rolls through a side door in the wall that he cannot see. Funny, bright.

slides.label: What I wrote
slides.caption: "branches: [main]". I read it as **"gate what reaches main"**.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout pins a neat sign-free shield above the main gate of a little castle and dusts off his leaf-hands, looking satisfied with a job well done, a cup of tea steaming on the battlements.

slides.myth: "Run the tests on anything heading for main."
slides.fact: It runs only when the pull request's **base** is main. Stacked on another branch? Skipped. Not failed.

slides.label: What it cost
slides.caption: Its first real run went **red immediately**. On a real bug.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout finally opens the side door of the castle wall and a huge pile of little bugs that had been waiting there for months tumbles out onto him in an avalanche; he is half buried, one leaf sticking out, eyes wide. Slapstick, funny.

slides.label: The same genre, in your setup

items.title: A cron job pointing at a renamed path
A monitor watching a hostname that stopped resolving
A test file excluded by a tightened glob

slides.text: Config that reads like intent can be a narrow filter. Quiet looks exactly like fine.
slides.save: 💾 Save this for your next CI review
